Company Description
The Joy Culture Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting Chinese language and culture in the San Francisco Bay Area. The organization provides educational and cultural programs and welcoming gathering spaces to help Mandarin-speaking families build confidence, identity, and community. It offers a comprehensive resource platform for families interested in Chinese culture, including Mandarin and English children’s books, a play space for children, and opportunities for parents to connect. Through bilingual Mandarin/English classes and programs, the foundation supports children’s immersion in Chinese culture and literacy while strengthening emotional connections between parents and children.

Key Responsibilities

1) Strategy & Mission Delivery
●     Lead multi-year strategic planning and annual operating plans that align programs and community needs while ensuring long-term financial sustainability and legal compliance
●     Deliver high-quality and meaningful programs that advance TJCF’s vision and create lasting community impact
●     Translate strategy into measurable goals, budgets, timelines, and outcomes
2) Organizational Leadership
●      Hire, coach, motivate, and retain a small, mission-aligned team, including core staff, teachers, and librarians
●     Champion a culture of community, kindness and teamwork
●      Develop volunteer leadership pipelines; recognize and grow community champions
3) Board Governance
●     Partner closely with the Board on strategy, policy, and performance; prepare timely reports and materials; run quarterly board meetings
●     Support Board development: recruitment, onboarding, committee engagement, and effective meetings.
4) Fundraising & Donor Relations
●     Own annual contributed-revenue goals across major gifts, grants, events, corporate sponsorships, and community giving
●     Build and manage a robust major donor pipeline; personally cultivate, solicit, and steward top prospects
●     Serve as primary spokesperson; strengthen brand, marketing, and media presence
●     Build partnerships with schools, libraries, civic organizations, cultural groups, and sponsors

Qualifications

●     10+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofits, education, libraries, museums, community development, or startups
●     Deep commitment to advancing TJCF’s mission and vision
●     Inspiring leader, communicator and relationship builder
●     Builder of teams, systems, and culture in resource-conscious environments
●     Strategic thinker who executes with discipline and clarity
●     Strong financial acumen
●     Adaptable, hands-on, and calm under pressure—comfortable switching between high-level strategy and day-to-day operations
●     Bilingual Mandarin/English
●     Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree a plus (MA, MPA, MBA, MLIS, or related).

About TJCF
The Joy Culture Foundation (TJCF) is a community-driven nonprofit dedicated to family learning and bilingual cultural enrichment. We operate the Little Bookworm Chinese Library
in Menlo Park and host high-impact community programs such as the Little Entrepreneur Fair
, seasonal cultural family days (CNY/Dragon Boat/Mid-Autumn), reading challenges, weekend classes, and youth leadership initiatives. Our vision is a welcoming, bilingual hub where families learn, connect, and thrive.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
About The Foster Museum

The Foster Museum is a 14,000-square-foot Palo Alto museum dedicated to the watercolor wilderness Journeys of British artist Tony Foster. Funded by the Foster Art & Wilderness Foundation, a 501(c)(3), we unite, understand, and share Foster’s work through our collection, archive, exhibitions, and programs to inspire connection to art, nature, and the protection of place. We’re a small core team supported by hourly staff and specialized consultants.

The Opportunity

The Foster Museum is at an inflection point, with an ambitious vision for its next chapter and a need for stronger infrastructure to support it. This is a newly created role, designed to build the operational foundation the museum needs for its next stage of growth. Some systems need thoughtful stewardship; others need to be built. We seek a Chief Operating Officer who is energized by both—creating practical systems and maintaining them as the museum grows.

The COO is responsible for the internal operations of the organization, owning people operations, finance, risk and compliance, facilities, capital projects, and cross-functional execution. This is a hands-on builder-operator role, with a strong onsite presence at the museum.

The Foster is a founder-led organization. The COO serves as the Executive Director’s key operational partner and has delegated authority across core operational functions, including management of the operating budget, vendor selection and contract execution, and development and implementation of operational policies and systems. The COO leads the organization’s internal operating cadence and serves as the Executive Director’s delegate in coordinating with staff, vendors, and partners. The role does not have formal direct reports at the outset. As the organization grows, supervisory responsibilities may be added to the position.

What You’ll Own

Broad by design: in each area, the COO builds what’s missing and maintains routines, documentation, and accountability staff can understand, use, and trust.

People & HR Operations

Steward our people-operations function as the go-to contact for routine staff and manager needs.
Turn HR groundwork from the Executive Director and external HR into durable processes, documentation, templates, and an annual people-and-compliance calendar. Run review, goal-setting, and compensation cycles; coordinate professional development.
Manage the employee lifecycle—recruiting, onboarding, benefits, offboarding—and keep personnel files, job descriptions, classifications, training, and HR policies current.
Coordinate employee relations, leave, accommodations, and compliance, escalating complex or high-risk matters to the Executive Director and outside HR/legal experts.
Own wage-and-hour compliance for hourly staff (classification, timekeeping, meal and rest breaks, overtime) with staff who handle scheduling.

Finance & Administration

Build the annual budget with the Executive Director; run a reliable forecasting, review, and decision-support cadence.
Review monthly financials and reconciliations, resolve discrepancies, and surface material issues.
Oversee the annual audit—documentation, timeline, and primary contact for our accountants and auditors.
Work with accounting, retirement-plan, and insurance partners on enrollment, renewals, claims, plan changes, and filings.
Own expenses and payment approvals: expense and card-use policies, organizational cards, and accurate coding.
Establish, maintain, and document internal financial controls.
Administer grant disbursements, reporting, and compliance documentation.
Assess earned income (private events, programs, retail) and identify opportunities.

Governance & Board Support

Prepare operational and financial Board reports with the Executive Director.
Maintain core governance records and the annual policy review.
Handle Board meeting logistics.

Operations, Compliance & Technology

Build manuals, workflows, and decision pathways that create clarity and preserve institutional knowledge.
Manage vendors and service contracts (expectations, terms, follow-through) and coordinate legal needs, including finding counsel.
Own technology, data, and security decisions with our IT partner, keeping systems and policies current, secure, and documented.
Oversee permits, licenses, and core records, coordinating filings with external partners.
Represent us with city departments and local stakeholders on site issues, including public meetings, coordinating solutions with the Executive Director.

Facilities & Capital Projects

Facilities will transition to this role over time, starting with capital and improvement projects.
Lead one-off capital projects (e.g., soundproofing, storage buildouts) from scoping and vendor selection to completion.
Take on facilities vendors, contracts, and budgets, with preventive maintenance, response protocols, and a multi-year operating and capital view.
Ensure security and emergency-preparedness systems are current, tested, and documented.

Potential Second Facility

The Foster is evaluating a potential second facility. If it proceeds, the COO leads its organizational and operational side and runs both sites; design, permitting, and construction stay with outside experts.
Keep a central source of truth for decisions, timelines, dependencies, owners, and documentation.
Run the project cadence: facilitate meetings, coordinate stakeholders, track commitments, and follow through.
Surface risks and decision points early.
Prepare and implement a two-site operating model.

What Success Looks Like

The Executive Director has a trusted operating partner who sees problems through.
People operations are planned, documented, and dependable, with a trusted internal contact and deliberate use of outside expertise.
Finance, compliance, technology, vendors, and facilities are reliable and visible; capital projects have clear ownership.
Staff know where to go and when to escalate; critical knowledge lives in durable systems, not just people’s heads.
The Executive Director’s capacity shifts to the museum’s direction, partnerships, and growth.

What You Bring

A builder and steward by nature, you create structure, improve systems that no longer serve, and maintain what works. You can build a budget or project plan, untangle an HR process, or find why things keep falling through the cracks. You see the whole system and dig into details when needed.

Experience & Skills

Meaningful operations ownership in a nonprofit, museum, foundation, small business, or similar setting, building or professionalizing durable systems. What you’ve owned matters more than years of experience.
A record of getting things done through people you don’t manage, building trust and accountability across staff and partners.
Strong financial fluency: budget development, review of externally prepared financials, and audit support.
Owning or building people operations in a small organization: HR administration, benefits, employee lifecycle, and outside experts.
Managing vendors, contracts, compliance, operational risk, and technology partners.
Excellent project management and communication across stakeholders, priorities, timelines, and decisions.

Preferred:
Bringing HR or operations in house; leading complex, multi-stakeholder projects; real estate or facilities experience; mission-driven work.

How You Work

Ownership and follow-through:
You notice what needs doing, make responsibilities and next steps visible, and close loops.
Humility and judgment:
You care more about the right answer than who had it, and know when to build a system, use a workaround, or escalate.
Curiosity and adaptability:
You ask good questions, learn quickly, and make progress while scope is still taking shape.
Equity and team orientation:
You notice whom a process or policy serves—and whom it may leave out—and bring warmth, perspective, and good humor to change.

If you don’t check every box but recognize yourself in the shape of this role, we’d still like to hear from you.

Position Details

Reporting:
This role reports to the Executive Director.
Anticipated Start:
December 2026 with flexibility for the right candidate.
Work Arrangement:
The Foster observes a museum-wide remote-work day on Mondays. The COO will work remotely on Mondays and onsite Tuesday through Friday at our Palo Alto museum. If a second facility (nearby) moves forward, the role will include time at that site.
Schedule:
Full-time and exempt, Monday through Friday during regular business hours. Occasional evening and weekend work is required for key museum events, Board meetings, contractor work, and urgent facilities or security matters.
After-Hours Availability:
As facilities responsibilities transition to the COO, this role will become a point of escalation for issues that genuinely cannot wait until regular business hours.
90-day Introductory Period:
This role includes a standard 90-day introductory period.

Benefits

100% employer-funded health, dental, and vision; company-paid life insurance; 401(k) with 6% match; public transit reimbursement; 20 vacation days, 11 holidays, and paid sick leave per applicable law.

Physical Requirements

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

Frequent desk work (extended sitting, typing, reading); regular movement through the museum and grounds, including stairs, storage, and back-of-house areas; occasional lifting up to 25 pounds, bending, reaching, kneeling, or step stool/ladder use during facilities walkthroughs and project oversight.

To Apply

Submit a resume and cover letter to careers@thefoster.org
with “Chief Operating Officer” in the subject line. Rolling review; priority consideration October 17, 2026.

The Foster Museum is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law.

Regional Director of Operations, West Coast

(Must reside within a commutable distance to LAX)

Our client has been in business for over 10 years but is still very much in an entrepreneurial and growth mindset. They have over 1200 employees, but still operate in a very “lean” fashion. In these + 10 years they have gone from $0 to $100M and are not slowing down. The right person for this position will bring a very “Can do” attitude and leadership skills that lead by example and are driven by success.

Our client is one of the top providers of transportation to the airline industry across the country. Reporting directly to the CEO, the Regional Director of Operations will be responsible for the successful day-to-day operations of the stations in his/her designated region. With direct oversight of the designated station leaders, the Regional Director of Operations will align teams through specified performance measures that achieve our service, safety, and financial goals. Further, the Regional Director of Operations will ultimately be responsible for managing delivery of the Company vision.

Ensures each station in region portfolio achieves Company financial goals. Regularly analyzes financial performance to ensure each station is on track to meet performance metrics.
Conducts monthly business reviews with each station leader across Company key performance indicators and adjusts plans with station leadership, as needed, to achieve results.
Develops quarterly business plans with each station leader to ensure each station is prepared and staffed for planned local events, as well as trained to execute during unplanned events that impact station operations.
Ensures all Station Leaders are executing effective scheduling practices: schedules posted on time, all trips covered according to contractual guidelines, proper LOD coverage, etc.

Develops succession plans for staffing needs and demonstrates a strong ability to recruit and develop others. Assesses talent at all levels and builds a bench of talent.
Identifies and develops designated trainers for station leaders and drivers within the region. Ensures that all new hires are effectively trained by certified trainer.
Effectively addresses performance issues and holds teams accountable in a constructive and timely manner. Appropriately partners with HR and elevates concerns with a sense of urgency.
Acts as point of escalation when service issues arise, advises station leaders on proper reporting and documentation. Ensures all complaints are answered with 24 hours.
Leverages data from observations and reported service issues to identify root cause and implement processes to improve execution in a measured way.
Engages station leaders to identify operational improvements in areas such as route optimization, fleet utilization, fuel expenditures, and routine maintenance costs.
Builds a best-in-class safety culture in region by leveraging training tools, employee engagement, recognition, and coaching. Ensures all safety policies are implemented and followed.
Ensures auditing of fuel cards, time and attendance, vehicle maintenance, office paperwork and record keeping, vehicle documents, etc. to maintain compliance with Company policy and mitigate risk and exposure.
Leads the fleet managers to ensure vehicle maintenance schedules are in place, correct number or vehicles are at each station, correct maintenance tools are present in stations/vans, and vehicles are maintained under the hood and inside the van as required.

Qualifications & Requirements

As a leader within the organization, the Regional Director of Operations must be passionate about customer service, have experience in the transportation, airline, hospitality, or retail industry. Other requirements include:
5-7 years of multi-unit leadership experience.
Flexible schedule to include nights and weekends as required to meet the needs of our 24/7/365 operation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to effectively communicate with all levels of the organization.
Strategic thinking and organizational skills that enable the ability to lead direct reports shoulder to shoulder, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
Strong leadership skills and the ability to work with employees from a variety of backgrounds, embrace diversity, promote inclusion, and motivate and develop a high performing team.
Extensive experience in P&L analysis and demonstrated problem-solving skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Travel Requirements – 50 – 75% travel required within assigned region and to headquarters, as needed.

Compensation:

Significant Salary commensurate with experience ($180K to $225K is the target, let’s discuss your qualifications and income expectations).
Significant and achievable bonus program at 25% of salary.

About Research And Analytics Division (RAD)

RAD is DCWP's in-house data team, and one of the first municipal offices of its kind in the country. Data scientists, technologists, engineers, product managers, and PhD economists work directly with the agency's attorneys and investigators to speed up investigations and win relief for consumers and workers. RAD also supports the agency's research, policy analysis, and public reporting. DCWP's data scientists and economists helped pioneer the Minimum Pay Rate for delivery workers, which has resulted in over $2 billion in additional pay. RAD will grow to 36 staff by FY28. It's hiring now, and it's moving fast.

The job

Companies hold the data that shows whether they broke the law. RAD is hiring three Executive Directors to lead the teams that sifts the data, decodes it, and turns it into evidence that wins in court. You will lead teams of data scientists, technologists, and engineers who work alongside DCWP's investigators and attorneys to hold businesses accountable to consumers and workers. In your area, you'll be the most senior technical person and the one accountable for getting the work right. You'll report to the Division's Associate Commissioner and partner with senior leaders across DCWP.

What you'll do

Casework. You supervise the technologists and data scientists on consumer and worker protection investigations and litigation. You work with investigators and attorneys to identify the data a case needs, and with businesses' counsel and technical staff to get it. Then you analyze it to describe business practices, evaluate compliance, and calculate damages, and present the findings to attorneys, in settlement negotiations, and in court.
Product. You decide what gets built. You work with attorneys, investigators, and case teams to gather requirements and design automated analytics products that assess business, consumer, and worker data for evidence of violations. You support users through deployment.
Engineering. You lead the engineers who build those products, through design, testing, and iteration.
Tech policy. Advise DCWP leadership on technology policy. Review laws and rules under consideration by the agency or the City Council to make sure they reflect how the technology works and can actually be enforced. Identify and push for new protections that have a strong technology component.

We’re a small core team supported by hourly staff and specialized consultants.

The Opportunity

The Foster Museum is at an inflection point, with an ambitious vision for its next chapter and a need for stronger infrastructure to support it. This is a newly created role, designed to build the operational foundation the museum needs for its next stage of growth. Some systems need thoughtful stewardship; others need to be built. We seek a Chief Operating Officer who is energized by both—creating practical systems and maintaining them as the museum grows.

The COO is responsible for the internal operations of the organization, owning people operations, finance, risk and compliance, facilities, capital projects, and cross-functional execution. This is a hands-on builder-operator role, with a strong onsite presence at the museum.

The Foster is a founder-led organization. The COO serves as the Executive Director’s key operational partner and has delegated authority across core operational functions, including management of the operating budget, vendor selection and contract execution, and development and implementation of operational policies and systems. The COO leads the organization’s internal operating cadence and serves as the Executive Director’s delegate in coordinating with staff, vendors, and partners. The role does not have formal direct reports at the outset. As the organization grows, supervisory responsibilities may be added to the position.

What You’ll Own

Broad by design: in each area, the COO builds what’s missing and maintains routines, documentation, and accountability staff can understand, use, and trust.

People & HR Operations

Steward our people-operations function as the go-to contact for routine staff and manager needs.
Turn HR groundwork from the Executive Director and external HR into durable processes, documentation, templates, and an annual people-and-compliance calendar. Run review, goal-setting, and compensation cycles; coordinate professional development.
Manage the employee lifecycle—recruiting, onboarding, benefits, offboarding—and keep personnel files, job descriptions, classifications, training, and HR policies current.
Coordinate employee relations, leave, accommodations, and compliance, escalating complex or high-risk matters to the Executive Director and outside HR/legal experts.
Own wage-and-hour compliance for hourly staff (classification, timekeeping, meal and rest breaks, overtime) with staff who handle scheduling.

Finance & Administration

Build the annual budget with the Executive Director; run a reliable forecasting, review, and decision-support cadence.
Review monthly financials and reconciliations, resolve discrepancies, and surface material issues.
Oversee the annual audit—documentation, timeline, and primary contact for our accountants and auditors.
Work with accounting, retirement-plan, and insurance partners on enrollment, renewals, claims, plan changes, and filings.
Own expenses and payment approvals: expense and card-use policies, organizational cards, and accurate coding.
Establish, maintain, and document internal financial controls.
Administer grant disbursements, reporting, and compliance documentation.
Assess earned income (private events, programs, retail) and identify opportunities.

Governance & Board Support

Prepare operational and financial Board reports with the Executive Director.
Maintain core governance records and the annual policy review.
Handle Board meeting logistics.

Operations, Compliance & Technology

Build manuals, workflows, and decision pathways that create clarity and preserve institutional knowledge.
Manage vendors and service contracts (expectations, terms, follow-through) and coordinate legal needs, including finding counsel.
Own technology, data, and security decisions with our IT partner, keeping systems and policies current, secure, and documented.
Oversee permits, licenses, and core records, coordinating filings with external partners.
Represent us with city departments and local stakeholders on site issues, including public meetings, coordinating solutions with the Executive Director.

Facilities & Capital Projects

Facilities will transition to this role over time, starting with capital and improvement projects.
Lead one-off capital projects (e.g., soundproofing, storage buildouts) from scoping and vendor selection to completion.
Take on facilities vendors, contracts, and budgets, with preventive maintenance, response protocols, and a multi-year operating and capital view.
Ensure security and emergency-preparedness systems are current, tested, and documented.

Potential Second Facility

The Foster is evaluating a potential second facility. If it proceeds, the COO leads its organizational and operational side and runs both sites; design, permitting, and construction stay with outside experts.
Keep a central source of truth for decisions, timelines, dependencies, owners, and documentation.
Run the project cadence: facilitate meetings, coordinate stakeholders, track commitments, and follow through.
Surface risks and decision points early.
Prepare and implement a two-site operating model.

What Success Looks Like

The Executive Director has a trusted operating partner who sees problems through.
People operations are planned, documented, and dependable, with a trusted internal contact and deliberate use of outside expertise.
Finance, compliance, technology, vendors, and facilities are reliable and visible; capital projects have clear ownership.
Staff know where to go and when to escalate; critical knowledge lives in durable systems, not just people’s heads.
The Executive Director’s capacity shifts to the museum’s direction, partnerships, and growth.

What You Bring

A builder and steward by nature, you create structure, improve systems that no longer serve, and maintain what works. You can build a budget or project plan, untangle an HR process, or find why things keep falling through the cracks. You see the whole system and dig into details when needed.

Experience & Skills

Meaningful operations ownership in a nonprofit, museum, foundation, small business, or similar setting, building or professionalizing durable systems. What you’ve owned matters more than years of experience.
A record of getting things done through people you don’t manage, building trust and accountability across staff and partners.
Strong financial fluency: budget development, review of externally prepared financials, and audit support.
Owning or building people operations in a small organization: HR administration, benefits, employee lifecycle, and outside experts.
Managing vendors, contracts, compliance, operational risk, and technology partners.
Excellent project management and communication across stakeholders, priorities, timelines, and decisions.

Preferred:
Bringing HR or operations in house; leading complex, multi-stakeholder projects; real estate or facilities experience; mission-driven work.

How You Work

Ownership and follow-through:
You notice what needs doing, make responsibilities and next steps visible, and close loops.
Humility and judgment:
You care more about the right answer than who had it, and know when to build a system, use a workaround, or escalate.
Curiosity and adaptability:
You ask good questions, learn quickly, and make progress while scope is still taking shape.
Equity and team orientation:
You notice whom a process or policy serves—and whom it may leave out—and bring warmth, perspective, and good humor to change.

If you don’t check every box but recognize yourself in the shape of this role, we’d still like to hear from you.

Position Details

Reporting:
This role reports to the Executive Director.
Anticipated Start:
December 2026 with flexibility for the right candidate.
Work Arrangement:
The Foster observes a museum-wide remote-work day on Mondays. The COO will work remotely on Mondays and onsite Tuesday through Friday at our Palo Alto museum. If a second facility (nearby) moves forward, the role will include time at that site.
Schedule:
Full-time and exempt, Monday through Friday during regular business hours. Occasional evening and weekend work is required for key museum events, Board meetings, contractor work, and urgent facilities or security matters.
After-Hours Availability:
As facilities responsibilities transition to the COO, this role will become a point of escalation for issues that genuinely cannot wait until regular business hours.
90-day Introductory Period:
This role includes a standard 90-day introductory period.

Benefits

100% employer-funded health, dental, and vision; company-paid life insurance; 401(k) with 6% match; public transit reimbursement; 20 vacation days, 11 holidays, and paid sick leave per applicable law.

Physical Requirements

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

Frequent desk work (extended sitting, typing, reading); regular movement through the museum and grounds, including stairs, storage, and back-of-house areas; occasional lifting up to 25 pounds, bending, reaching, kneeling, or step stool/ladder use during facilities walkthroughs and project oversight.

with “Chief Operating Officer” in the subject line. Rolling review; priority consideration October 17, 2026.

About Research And Analytics Division (RAD)

RAD is DCWP's in-house data team, and one of the first municipal offices of its kind in the country. Data scientists, technologists, engineers, product managers, and PhD economists work directly with the agency's attorneys and investigators to speed up investigations and win relief for consumers and workers. RAD also supports the agency's research, policy analysis, and public reporting. DCWP's data scientists and economists helped pioneer the Minimum Pay Rate for delivery workers, which has resulted in over $2 billion in additional pay. RAD will grow to 36 staff by FY28. It's hiring now, and it's moving fast.

The job

Companies hold the data that shows whether they broke the law. RAD is hiring three Executive Directors to lead the teams that sifts the data, decodes it, and turns it into evidence that wins in court. You will lead teams of data scientists, technologists, and engineers who work alongside DCWP's investigators and attorneys to hold businesses accountable to consumers and workers. In your area, you'll be the most senior technical person and the one accountable for getting the work right. You'll report to the Division's Associate Commissioner and partner with senior leaders across DCWP.

What you'll do

Casework. You supervise the technologists and data scientists on consumer and worker protection investigations and litigation. You work with investigators and attorneys to identify the data a case needs, and with businesses' counsel and technical staff to get it. Then you analyze it to describe business practices, evaluate compliance, and calculate damages, and present the findings to attorneys, in settlement negotiations, and in court.
Product. You decide what gets built. You work with attorneys, investigators, and case teams to gather requirements and design automated analytics products that assess business, consumer, and worker data for evidence of violations. You support users through deployment.
Engineering. You lead the engineers who build those products, through design, testing, and iteration.
Tech policy. Advise DCWP leadership on technology policy. Review laws and rules under consideration by the agency or the City Council to make sure they reflect how the technology works and can actually be enforced. Identify and push for new protections that have a strong technology component.
Team Management: Hire, supervise, and develop your team.

About DCWP

The NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) protects and enhances the daily economic lives of New Yorkers to create thriving communities. DCWP licenses nearly 45,000 businesses in more than 40 industries and enforces key consumer protection and workplace laws that apply to countless more. By supporting businesses through equitable enforcement and access to resources, DCWP protects the marketplace from predatory practices and strives to create a culture of compliance. DCWP empowers consumers and working families by providing the tools and resources they need to achieve financial health and work-life balance. DCWP also conducts research and advocates for public policy that furthers its work to support New York City’s communities. For more information about DCWP and its work, call 311 or visit DCWP at NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), sign up for its newsletter, or follow on its social media sites, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.

POSITION SUMMARY

The President & Chief Executive Officer serves as the chief executive officer and manager of the Greater Pasco Chamber of Commerce ("GPCC") and is responsible for the overall leadership, administration, financial management, staff management, membership development, community engagement, and daily operations of the organization.

The President/CEO works under the direction of the Board of Directors and, together with the Board Chair, is responsible for implementing GPCC's strategic direction, annual business plan, policies, programs, and organizational priorities.

The President/CEO serves as an advisor to the Board of Directors, Executive Committee, and officers of GPCC but shall not serve as a voting member of the Board or Executive Committee.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Board Governance & Strategic Leadership

The President/CEO shall:
Serve as the principal executive advisor to the Board of Directors, Executive Committee, and officers of GPCC.
Work closely with the Board Chair to implement the strategic plan, annual business plan, and priorities established by the Board.
Keep the Board informed of significant organizational, financial, operational, membership, and community developments.
Assemble and prepare reports, data, and other information requested by the Board or required under the annual business plan.
Assist with the preparation and maintenance of Board and organizational records, including notices, agendas, minutes, policies, and other official records.
Carry out other duties, responsibilities, and authorities assigned by the Board of Directors.

Organizational & Staff Management

Subject to the authority and policies of the Board of Directors, the President/CEO shall:
Be responsible for the overall administration and daily operations of GPCC.
Recruit, hire, supervise, evaluate, discipline, develop, and, when necessary, terminate GPCC employees.
Establish employee responsibilities, performance expectations, and organizational accountability.
Promote a professional, collaborative, ethical, and member-focused organizational culture.
Ensure appropriate staffing and allocation of organizational resources.
Ensure GPCC operations comply with Board-approved policies and applicable requirements.

Financial Management

The President/CEO shall:
Work with the Finance Committee and Treasurer to prepare an annual operating budget covering all activities of GPCC.
Present the proposed annual budget to the Board of Directors for approval.
Be responsible for organizational expenditures within Board-approved budget allocations and established financial policies.
Regularly monitor revenue, expenses, cash flow, membership revenue, sponsorships, events, and other financial indicators.
Assist the Treasurer and Finance Committee with the preparation and maintenance of accurate financial records and reports.
Identify opportunities to increase and diversify organizational revenue.
Maintain appropriate financial controls and accountability for Chamber resources.

Membership Development & Engagement

The President/CEO shall:
Develop and implement strategies for membership recruitment, engagement, and retention.
Maintain relationships with current and prospective Chamber members.
Regularly evaluate the benefits, programs, and services provided to members.
Identify opportunities to increase the value of GPCC membership.
Encourage member participation in Chamber events, committees, programs, and leadership opportunities.
Track and report membership performance and trends to the Board.

Community Relations & Communications

The President/CEO shall:
Serve as a principal public representative and spokesperson for GPCC.
Coordinate and conduct external communications except for specific responsibilities assigned by the Board to others.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with businesses, community organizations, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders.
Represent GPCC at appropriate community meetings, events, programs, and business functions.
Communicate Board-approved Chamber positions and priorities to appropriate stakeholders.
Maintain a visible and professional presence throughout the Greater Pasco community and Tampa Bay region.

Programs, Events & Partnerships

The President/CEO shall:
Provide executive oversight of GPCC programs, events, committees, networking activities, and member initiatives.
Evaluate programs and events for effectiveness, financial performance, member participation, and alignment with the Chamber's mission.
Identify opportunities for new programs, partnerships, sponsorships, and initiatives.
Develop relationships that expand GPCC's reach, influence, membership, and organizational sustainability.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration, Public Administration, Communications, Marketing, Nonprofit Management, Economic Development, or a related discipline.
Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible professional leadership experience.
Minimum of three to five years of senior management or executive leadership experience.
Demonstrated experience supervising and developing employees.
Demonstrated experience managing organizational budgets and financial performance.
Experience developing relationships with business, community, and organizational leaders.
Demonstrated experience in revenue development, membership development, sponsorships, fundraising, business development, or comparable activities.

Equivalent combinations of relevant education and significant executive-level experience may be considered at the discretion of the Board of Directors.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, Organizational Leadership, or a related field.
Executive leadership experience with a chamber of commerce, membership association, economic development organization, nonprofit organization, or similar organization.
IOM, CCE, CAE, or another relevant professional credential.
Knowledge of Pasco County and the Tampa Bay regional business environment.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

The President/CEO must demonstrate:
Executive leadership and strategic planning abilities.
Strong financial and organizational management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong public speaking and presentation abilities.
Exceptional interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Ability to work effectively with a volunteer Board of Directors.
Ability to develop and maintain relationships with diverse community stakeholders.
Ability to supervise, motivate, and hold employees accountable.
Strong organizational and time-management abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and projects simultaneously.
Sound professional judgment and discretion.
High standards of integrity, professionalism, confidentiality, and accountability.
Ability and willingness to attend meetings, events, and community activities outside normal business hours when required.

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

The President/CEO and Board of Directors shall establish annual performance goals and measurable objectives.
Performance measures may include:
Membership growth and retention.
Member engagement and satisfaction.
Financial performance and budget management.
Sponsorship and non-dues revenue development.
Program and event performance.
Community engagement and organizational visibility.
Development of strategic partnerships.
Implementation of the annual business and strategic plans.
Staff performance and development.
Completion of Board-directed initiatives.

The Board shall conduct a periodic performance evaluation of the President/CEO based upon these responsibilities and mutually established performance objectives.

COMPENSATION

The President/CEO is a salaried, exempt employee.
Initial compensation shall be established by the Board of Directors based upon the selected candidate's education, experience, qualifications, and negotiated employment terms.
The President/CEO may be eligible for an annual performance-based bonus pursuant to a bonus plan and measurable performance objectives approved by the Board of Directors.

PAID TIME OFF

The GPCC fiscal year begins July 1 and ends June 30.
In addition to paid holidays established by the GPCC Employee Policy and Procedure Manual, the President/CEO shall be entitled to  four weeks (20 business days) of paid vacation, personal, or sick leave ("PTO") per fiscal year
.

PTO encompassing more than two consecutive weeks (10 consecutive business days) requires approval of the GPCC Executive Board.

Unused PTO may roll over from year to year up to a maximum of two weeks (10 business days). PTO exceeding the maximum allowable rollover shall be forfeited.
At no time shall the President/CEO be entitled to more than six weeks (30 business days) of accumulated PTO.

Earned but unused PTO will not be paid upon resignation or termination except where otherwise required by applicable law.

Prior to the beginning of each fiscal year, the President/CEO shall provide the Board Chair and Executive Committee with a record of PTO utilized during the preceding fiscal year and confirm the PTO balance available for the upcoming year.

WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

The President/CEO is expected to maintain effective working relationships with:
GPCC Board of Directors and Executive Committee
GPCC employees
Chamber members and prospective members
Business and community leaders
Educational institutions
Nonprofit and community organizations
Regional chambers and business organizations
Sponsors and community partners
Media and other external stakeholders

Regional Director of Operations | Pacific Northwest

Location:
Based in the Pacific Northwest, preferably near Seattle or Chehalis, Washington, or Portland, Oregon. Candidates near Spokane or Pasco, Washington, or Boise, Idaho, may also be considered.

Travel:
Significant travel across the region, particularly during the first three to six months.
We are seeking a Regional Director of Operations to lead six branches across Washington, Oregon, and Idaho. This leader will oversee regional performance, develop branch managers, and bring greater consistency to an established operation. The role reports to the Chief Operating Officer and leads an organization of approximately 60 employees.

What you’ll do

Coach and develop branch operations managers, establish clear expectations, and build leadership depth.
Own regional P&L performance, budgets, margins, labor productivity, material spending, and asset utilization.
Use operating reviews and scorecards to identify issues, take corrective action, and track results.
Improve fleet readiness, inventory accuracy, facility standards, and asset refurbishment.
Oversee regional safety, fleet and DOT practices, and applicable prevailing wage processes.
Partner with sales and construction teams on forecasting, project handoffs, customer commitments, and capacity.
Standardize effective processes across branches while addressing each location’s needs.

What you bring

At least 10 years of progressive operations leadership experience, including responsibility for multiple locations.
Experience leading sizable teams and developing managers.
P&L and budget ownership in a branch-based, asset-heavy business.
Experience using performance measures to improve operational results.
Working knowledge of fleet or asset operations.
Ability to travel regularly throughout the Pacific Northwest.

Experience in mobile or modular structures, equipment rental, transportation, manufacturing, construction, or industrial services is especially relevant. Experience with EOS, DOT compliance, work order systems, or continuous improvement is helpful. A bachelor’s degree is preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.
Compensation and benefits

Base salary:
$100,000–$140,000 annually
Bonus:
Eligible for an annual performance bonus targeted at 25%
Health:
Medical, prescription, dental, and vision coverage options; a health savings account with the eligible medical plan
Time off:
80 hours of PTO in the first year, 7.5 paid holidays, two floating holidays, and eight hours of paid community service time annually
Retirement:
401(k) with company match and discretionary profit sharing
Additional benefits:
Company paid life insurance, short and long term disability coverage, and an employee assistance program
Role benefit:
Company vehicle and gas card
Other perks:
Wellness incentives, a $25 monthly exercise subsidy, charitable donation matching, and development and training opportunities

new_jobs.description:

What We Seek:

The University of New Mexico Foundation is seeking a dynamic, relationship-driven Director of Development to support philanthropic growth for UNM Hospitals and UNM Children’s Hospital. This position plays a critical role in advancing strategic fundraising priorities, deepening donor engagement, and partnering with Hospital leadership to build a culture of philanthropy that strengthens health care for communities across New Mexico.

What We Require:

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of securing major gifts, managing a donor portfolio, and building strong, long-term relationships. Strong written and verbal communication skills are essential, along with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and demonstrate a high level of professionalism and initiative. Candidates should possess experience using CRM systems for donor management, maintain strong organizational skills, and hold a valid driver’s license with the ability to travel for donor meetings and events.

The minimum education and experience required:
Baccalaureate degree
At least 3 years of successful fundraising and development experience, preferably in higher education/academic health care clinical institution.

Compensation Salary Range:

The expected salary for this position is $80,000 - $93,000. This range is an estimate, and the final salary will be determined based on the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications, consideration of any approved geographic salary differential, and alignment with internal equity guidelines to ensure consistency across similar roles.

Why Join the Foundation:

The UNM Foundation is a diverse, inclusive, and mission-driven community dedicated to advancing the University’s impact through research, education, and service. Our staff collaborate with passionate development professionals and enjoy competitive benefits, including healthcare, professional development, flexible paid leave, paid holidays, wellness programs, and strong retirement contributions. We value diverse perspectives and unique experiences, fostering a welcoming environment where you can make a lasting difference in New Mexico and beyond.
